## 06/10/2026 17:58 — Yes, these are different Sarvam surfaces

Partner, **your two new screenshots make it clear**. My previous explanation mixed up the products.

### What you actually have

**Screenshot 1 — browser (`indus.sarvam.ai`)**

You're inside **Sarvam API / developer platform**. It shows:

- API Keys
- MCP
- Model Catalogue
- Usage
- Billing
- your **62,335 credits**
- and the icons along the bottom switch between Sarvam products.

Sarvam's current documentation confirms that the web platform contains multiple product areas, including **Model APIs, Voice Agents, Content Studio and Doc Agents**. citeturn0search0

**Screenshot 2 — Google Play**

That's **Indus by Sarvam**, the Android application.

Indus is primarily Sarvam's **AI assistant/chat experience**, powered by Sarvam-105B. Sarvam describes that model as powering “Indus, Sarvam’s AI assistant for complex reasoning and agentic workflows.” citeturn0search9

So **Android Indus ≠ the entire Sarvam web platform**.

### Most important for your original question

You were asking:

> **Where has speaker splitting/transcription gone?**

Don't look for it inside the Android Indus app.

On your **browser screenshot**, use the product navigation at the bottom and get to the **Speech-to-Text/API playground or Content Studio**.

There is also current evidence from September 2026 showing Sarvam's web Speech-to-Text playground at:

urlSarvam Speech-to-Text playgroundhttps://indus.sarvam.ai/api-playground/speech-to-text

and Sarvam's newer Content Studio at:

urlSarvam Content Studiohttps://indus.sarvam.ai/creator-studio

The Speech-to-Text route is specifically reported as supporting the **diarize/transcribe workflow — identifying who spoke and when**. citeturn0search4

**So don't uninstall or troubleshoot the Android app. It's simply not a 1:1 mobile version of everything on the Sarvam website.**

If your goal right now is your **Tamil meeting audio + Speaker 1 / Speaker 2 separation**, open the **Speech-to-Text playground link above in Chrome**. That's the route I'd use first.

## 06/10/2026 17:56 — Sarvam app vs website

Yes — **your screenshot explains the confusion**.

What you're looking at in the Android app is **Sarvam's newer Cowork/Work Agents interface**, not the **Content Studio transcription interface** I was describing.

Your screenshot has:

**New chat · Agents · Skills · Knowledge base · Connectors · Scheduled tasks**

Those are exactly the components Sarvam documents for **Cowork**. citeturn0search0turn0search4

Sarvam currently has several different products/interfaces under the same account:

| Sarvam area | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Cowork** | Chat, Agents, Skills, Connectors, scheduled work |
| **Content Studio** | **Audio transcription**, dubbing, speech/voice |
| **Voice Agents** | Build phone/chat agents |
| **Doc Agents** | Documents/OCR/translation |
| **Model APIs** | Developer APIs |

Sarvam's own current platform documentation explicitly describes **Content Studio** as the place to “transcribe audio from the browser.” citeturn0search6

### So where did your speaker-split option go?

It probably **hasn't disappeared from Sarvam transcription**. You're simply in a different Sarvam product in this screenshot.

For your Tamil `.ogg` recording, I would **not use this Cowork screen**.

Use the **web browser → Sarvam platform → Content Studio → Transcribe**, where we can then check whether the **speaker diarization / speaker labels** option is available.

And this explains why you remembered Sarvam differently: **the website you previously used for transcription and this Android app are not presenting the same product surface.**

If you show me a screenshot of the **Sarvam website transcription page you're seeing now**, I can check **exactly where the speaker-split setting has moved** rather than guessing.

## 06/10/2026 17:52 — Sarvam speaker split

Yes, partner — **Sarvam AI still has speaker splitting (speaker diarization)**. It has **not been removed**.

The important change/limitation is **where you're transcribing**.

Sarvam's current documentation says:

| Method | Speaker split / diarization |
|---|---|
| **Batch Speech-to-Text** | ✅ Yes |
| REST Speech-to-Text | ❌ No |
| Realtime/Streaming | ❌ No |
| Sarvam web transcription UI | ✅ Yes — **Diarization / “Detect and label speakers”** toggle |

citeturn0search0turn0search2turn0search6

### If you're using the Sarvam website

After **uploading the audio file**, Sarvam says the screen should show:

**Language → Mode → Diarization**

and the toggle is labelled **“Detect and label speakers.”** citeturn0search2

So if you're **not seeing that option now**, tell me **which Sarvam screen/page you're on** (or send me a screenshot). I can check the exact current interface and tell you where it moved.

### For your Tamil meeting recording

This is exactly what you want:

**Tamil audio → Batch transcription → Diarization ON → speaker-separated Tamil transcript**

The output can contain entries like:

```text
Speaker 0:
...

Speaker 1:
...

Speaker 0:
...
```

with start/end timestamps. Sarvam currently supports **up to 20 speakers**, and it can automatically determine the number if you don't specify it. citeturn0search0

So for the **Tamil `.ogg` meeting recording you were trying to transcribe earlier today**, Sarvam's Batch + Diarization route looks like a very suitable workaround. memcite
